evidence_summary: In March 2025 the SBTi validated ING's 1.5°C-aligned emission-reduction targets for fossil fuels, power, cement, steel, automotive, aviation and commercial real estate. The validated targets cover 67% of ING's financed emissions (reference year 2021).
quote: In March 2025, ING became the first global systemically important bank to receive validation from the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) for 1.5°C-aligned targets.
notes: See also p. 92.

evidence_summary: ING reports a combined own-operations footprint (Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 business travel) of 44 kt CO2 for 2025, and separately reports PCAF financed emissions (Scope 3 category 15).
quote: In 2025, our total operations footprint (scopes 1, 2 and scope 3 business travel) was 44kt of CO2 emissions
notes: Own operations were assessed as not material in the DMA (p. 357), so the footprint sits outside the ESRS statement and Scope 1 and 2 are not shown separately. Methodology on p. 350; footprint under limited assurance (p. 346). Financed emissions on pp. 125-126.

evidence_summary: ING calculates financed emissions with the PCAF methodology for EUR 704.5 bn of lending and investments (mortgages, commercial real estate, corporate lending, bonds and equity), covering clients' Scope 1, 2 and 3.
quote: Clients’ Scope 1 & 2 Clients’ Scope 3 (upstream & downstream emissions) … Total financing 704.5 647.7 Financing not in scope of financed emissions 187.5 202.2 … [p. 125] Both metrics are calculated in accordance with the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF) methodology to ensure transparency and comparability.
notes: EUR 187.5 bn is out of scope (money market instruments, pre-settlement, consumer lending other than mortgages), see p. 125. Weighted PCAF data-quality scores are around 4 on a 1-5 scale (5 = least precise).

evidence_summary: ING's 2025 turnover-based Green Asset Ratio is 14% (EUR 66 bn aligned out of EUR 458 bn covered assets), driven mainly by mortgages; 87% of covered assets are taxonomy-eligible.
quote: For 2025, our GAR based on Turnover is 14 percent (2024: 7 percent).
notes: Category follows the agreed GAR thresholds (medium = 10-25%). The 2025 GAR uses the amended Delegated Act denominator; on the old basis 2024 was 7%, and ING says the ratio was stable like-for-like.

evidence_summary: ING treats ESG risk as a driver across credit, compliance, non-financial and business risk, governed by an ESG Risk Committee. It quantifies the risk with a physical-risk tool, a client-level transition-risk scorecard and climate stress tests, and limits it through risk appetite statements.
quote: Transition risk scorecard: Used by ING to quantify transition risk with a scorecard approach at client-level. … ING continues enhancing its climate stress-testing methodology to assess the impact of climate risks on corporate and mortgage exposures from a credit risk perspective under different climate scenarios. … This pool of high-risk clients is subsequently managed via the climate risk-appetite setting.
notes: See pp. 205-207 (risk mapping) and p. 209 (risk appetite and mitigation).

evidence_summary: ING aims to phase out financing for upstream oil and gas by 2040 and to exit utilities with more than 5% thermal-coal activity by end-2025 (one EU client remained above the threshold); exposure to coal-fired plants fell 86% since 2017.
quote: For the oil and gas sector, ING aims to phase-out its financing to upstream oil and gas exploration and production by 2040 … it is our policy to phase out financing for clients in the utilities sector that derive more than 5 percent of their activities from thermal coal by the end of 2025.
notes: From 2026 ING no longer finances new LNG export terminals (p. 115). Not 'exit' because the oil and gas phase-out is a 2040 target, not yet in effect.

evidence_summary: ING sets annual gender targets for leadership and reports progress: women held 35% of senior positions in 2025 (2024: 32%). It discloses an unadjusted gender pay gap of 27% and an adjusted gap of 3%.
quote: Targets are set on an annual basis, reviewed and approved by the management boards and Supervisory Board. … In 2025, the number of women in senior positions (GJA 22+) was 35 percent, up from 32 percent in 2024. … [p. 138] For 2025, using annual fixed remuneration and target bonus, the unadjusted gender pay gap of ING globally was 27 percent.
notes: Pay-gap figures on p. 138.

evidence_summary: ING has policies against discrimination, harassment and violence, a whistleblower channel with human-rights categories, and reports no severe human-rights incidents in its workforce in 2025. Employees are represented through Dutch works councils and a European Works Council.
quote: Based on our assessment, no severe human rights incidents connected to our own workforce were identified in the reporting period (2024: nil). … [p. 90] ING also has a cross-border European Works Council (EWC), which is consulted when decisions are made that affect employees in multiple countries. … [p. 358] S1-8 Collective bargaining coverage and social dialogue Based on our DMA outcome, this requirement is not applicable
notes: Works councils on p. 90. Collective bargaining coverage, adequate wages and health and safety metrics are not reported; the DMA marks them not applicable (p. 358). That gap is why this is 'medium', not 'strong'.

evidence_summary: ING introduced a global Customer Centricity Policy in 2024 (updated in 2025) with minimum standards for product approval, clear information and complaints handling. Compensation for Dutch revolving consumer credit with variable rates was substantially completed in 2025 but continues into 2026.
quote: After rolling out the first version of the CCP in 2024, we updated the policy this year to bring elements such as discrimination and access to banking into the Compliance Risk Framework. … [p. 311] The compensation process is still ongoing and may take until Q2 2026.
notes: Revolving-credit compensation and provisions (EUR 180 m in 2021, EUR 75 m in 2022) on p. 311. Ongoing customer litigation in Spain (mortgage expenses) and Poland (CHF mortgages) on p. 310. No regulatory customer-treatment fine disclosed for 2023-2025.

evidence_summary: ING reports that it completed its multi-year KYC Enhancement Programme and in 2025 moved from building foundations to keeping controls operationally effective, under second-line oversight.
quote: This evolution is supported by the completion of the multi-year KYC Enhancement Programme, which strengthened our customer due diligence and transaction monitoring capabilities. … In 2025, our focus has shifted from foundational maturity to maintaining operational effectiveness, with oversight and challenge from the second line of defence.
notes: The 2018 settlement with the Dutch Public Prosecution Service is outside the 2023-2025 window (p. 309). A Luxembourg AML criminal case was cleared for trial in December 2025 (p. 309); it is captured in the controversy row. Alternative reading: 'building'.

evidence_summary: The Supervisory Board states that all of its members were independent under the Dutch Corporate Governance Code and NYSE standards on 31 December 2025.
quote: On this basis, the SB confirms that all members of the SB are to be regarded as independent on 31 December 2025.
notes: Two-tier board: independence measured on the Supervisory Board.

evidence_summary: The Supervisory Board has a dedicated ESG Committee that advises on ESG strategy, integration and disclosures using an ESG dashboard. The management boards are accountable for ESG, supported by an ESG Risk Committee.
quote: The ESG Committee assists the SB with matters relating to the various areas of ESG, including but not limited to, the development of ESG and its integration in the company
notes: SB ESG Committee also described on p. 206.

evidence_summary: In the CEO's 2025 variable-pay scorecard, environment targets weigh 10% and social targets 5% (15% in total); the CFO and CRO also have 15%.
notes: At least 50% of variable-pay metrics must be non-financial (p. 67), but most of that weight is customer, risk and strategy targets. Variable pay is capped at 20% of fixed pay.

evidence_summary: ING published its second sustainability statement prepared under ESRS, and the external auditor issued an unmodified limited-assurance conclusion on ESRS and EU Taxonomy (Article 8) compliance.
quote: nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe that the Sustainability statement is not, in all material respects: prepared in accordance with the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS)
notes: Basis of preparation on p. 93: Dutch transposition of the CSRD was still pending and is expected to apply retroactively. Some datapoints are omitted under ESRS phase-in provisions (e.g. E1-9, p. 357).

evidence_summary: Several ESG-related legal matters were ongoing in 2025: Milieudefensie filed a climate lawsuit against ING in March 2025, and a Luxembourg court cleared an AML criminal case against ING Luxembourg for trial in December 2025. No new fine or settlement was disclosed for 2025.
quote: In March 2025, Milieudefensie started legal proceedings at the Court in Amsterdam against ING by serving the writ of summons. … [p. 309] In December 2025, the Court of Appeal upheld the first decision without making any substantive changes, as a result of which the case can now be heard before the Tribunal Correctionnel.
notes: Luxembourg case and investor claims over past financial-crime shortcomings (rejected in November 2025, appealed in February 2026) on p. 309.

evidence_summary: ABN AMRO sets sector decarbonisation targets mostly against 1.5°C science-based benchmarks such as the IEA NZE scenario, but states that its climate targets have not been validated by an independent external body.
quote: For all sectors apart from agriculture and commercial real estate, we have chosen science-based benchmarks that are aligned with the latest 1.5°C scenario reference pathways. … The climate targets have not been validated by an independent external body.
notes: Some 2030 targets (residential mortgages, commercial real estate, inland shipping, road transport) sit above the reference pathway (p. 220). Targets cover 18% of total financed emissions (p. 221). Agriculture follows a Dutch national pathway rather than a 1.5°C scenario.

evidence_summary: ABN AMRO reports own-operations Scope 1, Scope 2 (market- and location-based) and Scope 3 (business travel and commuting) emissions as separate lines, and reports PCAF financed emissions (Scope 3 category 15) in its climate section.
quote: Total scope 1 emissions 2,025 1,084 … Total scope 2 location-based emissions 8,502 7,224 … Total scope 3 emissions 20,731 17,419
notes: The own-operations table sits in the ESG Annex, which is outside the ESRS statements and outside the limited assurance (p. 287). Financed emissions on p. 243.

evidence_summary: ABN AMRO calculates financed emissions with PCAF for EUR 301 bn of assets (mortgages, corporate loans, financial investments including sovereign bonds, and some consumer loans), reporting clients' Scope 1, 2 and 3; the total was 29,680 ktCO2e in 2025.
quote: The lending portfolio’s GHG emissions are calculated in accordance with the principles set by PCAF. … The GHG tables above provide an overview of the assets that are in scope of GHG emission reporting and the Partnership Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF) data quality score.
notes: 71% of total assets are in scope (p. 244). Average PCAF data-quality score 3.4 for Scope 1 and 2 (1-5 scale, 5 = least precise). Assets out of scope have no PCAF methodology.

evidence_summary: ABN AMRO's 2025 turnover-based Green Asset Ratio (stock) is 21% (EUR 40.6 bn aligned), calculated with the amended Delegated Act denominator.
quote: resulting in an increase of ABN AMRO’s main KPI GAR from 11% (31 December 2024) to 21%.
notes: On the previous methodology the GAR would be 12% (2024: 11%). Category follows the agreed GAR thresholds (medium = 10-25%). ING's 14% uses the same amended basis, so the two are comparable.

evidence_summary: ABN AMRO maps ESG risk drivers to all traditional risk types, identifies them with environmental and social risk heatmaps and stress testing, and sets an ESG risk appetite with key risk indicators and limits monitored quarterly.
quote: The ESG risk appetite is defined through key risk indicators (KRIs), which address ESG factors and risks. … To ensure ESG risks remain within the approved risk appetite, we set limits and checkpoints and monitor them quarterly at the bank-wide, entity and local levels. … [p. 210] ESG risk takes effect in the form of ESG risk drivers and their subsequent transmission channels, affecting the traditional financial and non-financial risk types. … [p. 214] These heatmaps inform, for example, the materiality assessment (see the Strategy and business model section for more on impact and financial materiality assessment), the internal stress testing and the risk appetite
notes: Risk-driver mapping on p. 210; scenario analysis and stress testing on pp. 211 and 214.

evidence_summary: ABN AMRO commits to phase out thermal coal by 2030 (with exceptions for German plants due to close under the national coal exit law) and excludes direct lending to oil and gas fields licensed after 2023. Its upstream oil and gas commitments fell to EUR 566 m in 2025 (2024: EUR 804 m).
quote: ABN AMRO is dedicated to phasing out thermal coal by 2030, and includes requirements for coal-fired power generation companies in the ESG Risk Standard with Client Requirements. … We continued to exclude direct lending to oil and gas fields licensed for development after 2023. … our oil and gas upstream commitments continued to decline over the past year, from EUR 804 million in 2024 to EUR 566 million in 2025.
notes: No phase-out date for upstream oil and gas: the 2030 target is EUR 987 m of committed financing (2021 baseline EUR 1,268 m), already met (p. 223). Under the agreed definition this is 'partial' (dated phase-out for coal only); 'strong' would need a dated oil and gas phase-out.

evidence_summary: ABN AMRO sets gender targets (48% women in the Extended Leadership Team, 35% in senior and middle management) and cultural-diversity targets, and reports progress; women held 34% of Extended Leadership Team roles in 2025, below target.
quote: Women currently represent 34% of the Extended Leadership Team against a 48% ambition, with senior and middle management representation also below the 35% target. … [p. 258] Gender pay gap 18% 16% Employees with occupational disability
notes: Gender pay gap 18% (2024: 16%) on p. 258; the increase is partly a calculation change (p. 260). The category reflects targets and disclosure, not whether targets were met.

evidence_summary: ABN AMRO discloses collective bargaining coverage of 93% of employees (97.6% in the Netherlands, where 99.8% are covered by workers' representatives), and reports no severe human-rights violations and no related fines in 2025.
quote: The outcome of this metric is 93.17%. This percentage reflects that the Netherlands, Brazil, France, Germany and Belgium each have a CLA in place … [p. 261] In 2025, ABN AMRO did not register any severe human rights violations, including non-compliance with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights
notes: No severe violations on p. 261. Human-rights approach based on the UNGPs and OECD Guidelines (p. 288). Total incidents from speak-up channels are not disclosed for 2025 (p. 261).

evidence_summary: ABN AMRO completed its compensation scheme for revolving consumer credit with variable interest in 2025, using EUR 483 m of a provision of about EUR 505 m. Its product approval, duty-of-care and complaints policies set minimum standards for customer treatment.
quote: The execution of the compensation scheme has been completed in 2025 and the handling of any other matters relating to consumer credits with a variable interest rate has been handed over
notes: Policies on pp. 264-265. Pending duty-of-care claims (p. 376) and an SME variable-rate collective action declared inadmissible in July 2025 but appealed (pp. 377-378). Not 'mature' because a large remediation ran in the 2023-2025 window; this matches the ING row.

evidence_summary: ABN AMRO's AML remediation programme was still running in 2025, and DNB had identified shortcomings in its EDR process that it said may lead to enforcement measures.
quote: ABN AMRO continues to enhance its internal AML processes and systems to increase both effectiveness and sustainable compliance with regulatory requirements. … DNB has indicated that these shortcomings may lead to enforcement measures.
notes: The EUR 480 m settlement with the Dutch Public Prosecution Service (19 April 2021, https://www.abnamro.com/en/news/abn-amro-accepted-settlement) is outside the 2023-2025 window. After the reporting year, on 9 July 2026, DNB fined ABN AMRO EUR 8.5 m for due-diligence shortcomings on high-risk customers in files from September 2023 to September 2024 (https://www.abnamro.com/en/news/dnb-imposes-fine-on-abn-amro-for-shortcomings-in-part-of-anti-money-laundering-framework); if post-year events were counted this row would be 'fined'.

evidence_summary: The Supervisory Board confirms that all of its members are independent under the Dutch Corporate Governance Code.
quote: The Supervisory Board confirms that all members of the Supervisory Board are independent within the meaning of best practice provision 2.1.10 of the Dutch Corporate Governance Code.
notes: Two-tier board: independence measured on the Supervisory Board.

evidence_summary: The Supervisory Board has a Supervisory Sustainability Committee that advises on the sustainability aspects of strategy, the double materiality assessment and the climate strategy.
quote: The Supervisory Sustainability Committee advises the Supervisory Board on matters within the area of sustainability.
notes: In 2025 the Executive Board disbanded its management-level Group Sustainability Committee and spread its tasks across existing committees (pp. 148, 207).

evidence_summary: Under the Dutch bonus prohibition, Executive Board members are not entitled to variable remuneration and received only fixed pay for 2025, so no executive pay is linked to ESG targets.
quote: Due to the aforementioned bonus prohibition, the Executive Board members (and a specific group of senior staff) are not entitled to variable remuneration.
notes: This reflects a legal restriction, not a policy choice. Under the agreed definition (weight of E/S targets in the CEO's variable pay) the value is 0%, so 'none'. In 2025 DNB fined ABN AMRO EUR 15 m for violating the bonus prohibition in 2016-2024 (p. 378).

evidence_summary: ABN AMRO prepared its 2025 Sustainability Statements under the CSRD and ESRS, and the external auditor issued an unmodified limited-assurance conclusion on ESRS and EU Taxonomy (Article 8) compliance.
quote: nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe that the sustainability statement is not, in all material respects: prepared in accordance with the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS)
notes: Basis of preparation on p. 194. The ESG Annex (including the own-operations GHG table) is excluded from the assurance, and the client assets of the newly acquired HAL are not yet included (p. 194).

evidence_summary: In 2025 ABN AMRO paid a EUR 14 m fine to the Dutch Public Prosecution Service for involvement in transactions that, according to the prosecutor, were linked to intentionally incorrect tax returns filed in 2010-2013, and a EUR 15 m DNB fine for violating the bonus prohibition.
quote: For this imposed penalty order, ABN AMRO paid a fine of EUR 14 million. The other fine was imposed by the Dutch Central Bank (DNB) for violations of the bonus prohibition
notes: Tax-related financial crime counts as ESG-related under the agreed definition (ABN AMRO itself lists tax evasion as a financial-crime risk, p. 267); the DNB remuneration fine alone would not. Also ongoing: German cum/ex and cum/cum investigations (p. 376), AML-related investor claims (p. 378) and duty-of-care claims (p. 376).

evidence_summary: Rabobank sets GHG-reduction targets for 19 prioritised sector-region combinations, covering 61% of its financed emissions, using science-based pathways (e.g. SBTi FLAG, IEA NZE, CRREM) and the Dutch Climate Agreement. The targets are approved by the Managing Board; the report does not mention external validation.
quote: To achieve our 2050 goal, we set GHG emissions reduction targets for 19 prioritized sector x region combinations in our portfolio. … These targets cover a significant majority of the financed emissions of our portfolio (61%). … [p. 105] SBTi FLAG Rural Australia … [p. 105] IEA NZE Energy/Power Retail Netherlands … [p. 105] DCA: Dutch Climate Agreement
notes: Pathways per target on p. 105: Dutch agriculture targets follow the Dutch Climate Agreement rather than a 1.5°C scenario, and two leasing targets use an own methodology. No SBTi target validation is mentioned anywhere in the report.

evidence_summary: Rabobank reports operational emissions covering Scope 1, Scope 2 and part of Scope 3 (business travel, commuting, paper, fuel- and energy-related activities), 73,711 t CO2 in 2025, and reports PCAF financed emissions (Scope 3 categories 13 and 15).
quote: Currently, we report on our emissions in Scope 1, Scope 2, and some emissions in Scope 3 (i.e., paper consumption, fuel- and energy-related activities, business travel and employee commuting). … Rabobank's material impact is on the GHG emissions from our customers (Scope 3 emissions, category 13 and 15).
notes: Operational emissions are broken down by category (offices, data centres, vehicles, air travel) rather than by scope, and are disclosed voluntarily because own operations are not material in the DMA (p. 88). No market- or location-based Scope 2 split. Financed emissions on p. 97. Same category as ING for a similar combined disclosure.

evidence_summary: Rabobank reports PCAF financed emissions for 98% of relevant on-balance assets (73% of total assets), covering mortgages, Dutch business customers, Wholesale & Rural and international leasing; Scope 1 and 2 financed emissions were 42.0 Mt CO2e.
quote: This year we are able to report financed emissions for 98% (FY 2023: 99%) of the relevant (73% of our total assets (FY 2023: 73%)) on-balance sheet assets. … we observed a 10% decrease in our financed emissions (Scopes 1 and 2) on a comparable basis, from 46.9 Mt CO₂e to 42.0 Mt CO₂e. … [p. 99] In Rabobank we use the PCAF standard for accounting and disclosing financed emissions.
notes: Figures relate to the 2024 portfolio (one-year lag). Average PCAF data-quality score 3.6 for Scope 1 and 2 (p. 99); the Dutch Food & Agri portfolio averages 4.8 (p. 255). The auditor's emphasis of matter highlights high measurement uncertainty in these figures (p. 421).

evidence_summary: Rabobank's 2025 turnover-based Green Asset Ratio (stock) is 15.06% (EUR 34.1 bn aligned) under the amended Delegated Act, driven mainly by residential mortgages.
quote: Green asset ratio (GAR) stock 34,066 15.06%
notes: On the old basis the FY2024 GAR was about 4.6%; restated on the new basis it is 10.9% (p. 108). The large denominator effect comes from Rabobank's big exposure to non-CSRD counterparties (SMEs and non-EU clients). Category follows the agreed GAR thresholds (medium = 10-25%).

evidence_summary: Rabobank assesses climate- and nature-related ESG drivers for each risk type and runs NGFS-based resilience analysis and a group-wide climate stress test whose results feed into ICAAP and transition planning. It uses its risk appetite statement, including sector-specific limits, to steer the portfolio.
quote: We assess the impact of these ESG drivers on each risk type within our Risk Taxonomy. … The outcomes are integrated in key internal processes such as ICAAP and transition planning. … [p. 95] Risk Appetite Statement, e.g., changing our risk appetite for customers who are not compliant with our sustainability policy, sector-specific limits, etcetera.
notes: Risk appetite and sector-specific limits as a portfolio lever on p. 95; the ESG entry in the Group Risk Appetite Statement itself is qualitative (p. 53), and no quantified climate KRIs are disclosed (ABN AMRO discloses KRIs with quarterly limits). Treated like ING, whose evidence is similar. Alternative reading: 'full'.

evidence_summary: Rabobank's energy policy already excludes new financing of exploration and extraction of all fossil fuels, direct financing of thermal coal activities, and direct financing of non-conventional fossil activities.
quote: No new financing of exploration and extraction activities of all fossil fuels. … No direct financing of all thermal coal activities, higher-grade metallurgical coals are accepted (as recommended by SBTi & IEA). … No direct financing of all non-conventional fossil activities.
notes: Traded oil and gas financing continues, with a target to cut it by 20% by 2030 vs 2022 (p. 95). Clients with more than 5% thermal-coal turnover can still be financed if they reduce it to 0% by 2030 (developed countries) or 2040 (rest of world). If 'exit' should mean no fossil financing at all, this would be 'strong'.

evidence_summary: Rabobank sets a gender-diversity target for top management and reports progress, and discloses an unadjusted gender pay gap of 23.30% and an adjusted gap of 1.25%.
quote: Adjusted gender pay gap 1.25% 2024: 1.39%*/1.30% … Unadjusted gender pay gap 23.30% 2024: 24.26%*/20.00% … [p. 129] These targets concern gender diversity in top management and the engagement scan score.
notes: Targets described on p. 129; the gender pay gap methodology was refined in 2025 and comparatives restated (p. 129).

evidence_summary: Rabobank describes works council participation and collective labour agreement negotiations in the Netherlands, and internal channels that handled 734 HR cases in 2025; it states it is not aware of severe human-rights incidents in its own workforce.
quote: Rabobank carries out negotiations with trade unions on the collective labor agreement for the employees in the Netherlands. … In the Netherlands, the Works Council plays a vital role in ensuring employee participation and protecting their interests within Rabobank. … We currently have no internal registration of severe human rights issues and incidents in connection with our own workforce in the Netherlands, given that such complaints are not received. … [p. 124] S1-8 Collective bargaining coverage and social dialogue Not material
notes: Collective bargaining coverage, adequate wages and health and safety are marked 'Not material' and not reported (p. 124). Rabobank also says it has no registration of fines or compensation for severe human-rights incidents (p. 128). Same category as ING for the same gap.

evidence_summary: In 2025 Rabobank was still compensating customers whose consumer-credit interest rates had not been adjusted in line with the Kifid reference rate, sending letters to the remaining eligible customers (residual provision EUR 3.5 m).
quote: Rabobank is proactively compensating certain customers after not consistently adjusting interest rates on certain consumer credit products in line with the reference rate indicated by the Dutch Financial Services Complaints Tribunal (Kifid).
notes: Global standards on treating clients fairly, complaints handling and product governance on p. 140; complaints procedure on p. 142. Not 'mature' because customer remediation ran in the 2023-2025 window; this matches ING and ABN AMRO.

evidence_summary: Rabobank reports that it completed the remediation of AML compliance deficiencies under the DNB instruction and now focuses on embedding operationally effective controls.
quote: Following the completion of the remediation of compliance deficiencies related to the Dutch Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing Act … Rabobank has continued to embed and maintain robust, operationally effective controls within its day-to-day business processes.
notes: The Dutch Public Prosecutor has treated Rabobank as a suspect under the Wwft since December 2022, decided in April 2025 to prosecute, and sent a draft indictment in December 2025 (p. 327); this is captured in the controversy row, as for ING's Luxembourg case. Alternative reading: 'building'. A search on 17 October 2026 found no verdict, fine or settlement.

evidence_summary: The Supervisory Board states that its composition continued to meet the independence provisions 2.1.7 to 2.1.9 of the Dutch Corporate Governance Code in 2025.
quote: The Supervisory Board, in its current composition, continued to meet best practices provisions 2.1.7 thru 2.1.9 of the Dutch Corporate Governance Code, concerning requirements of independency.
notes: The report gives no count of independent members; the category relies on provision 2.1.7, under which fewer than half of the members may be non-independent. Two-tier board: measured on the Supervisory Board.

evidence_summary: The Supervisory Board's Cooperative and Sustainability Committee advises on sustainability ambitions, strategy and targets, and met five times in 2025.
quote: The Cooperative and Sustainability Committee assesses and advises the Supervisory Board on how Rabobank’s cooperative identity and sustainability ambitions translate into strategic direction, stakeholder expectations, and market developments. … In 2025, the Cooperative & Sustainability Committee convened five times.
notes: The committee combines sustainability with cooperative affairs. Board-level sustainability responsibilities also described on p. 73.

evidence_summary: Rabobank's Managing Board members do not receive variable remuneration, so no executive pay is linked to ESG targets.
quote: Our Managing Board members do not receive variable remuneration as part of their regular remuneration package.
notes: Unlike ABN AMRO, this is Rabobank's own remuneration policy rather than a legal ban. The 2025 remuneration table confirms 100% fixed pay (p. 161). Same category as ABN AMRO under the agreed definition.

evidence_summary: Rabobank's 2025 Sustainability Statements, prepared under ESRS, received an unmodified limited-assurance conclusion from the external auditor on ESRS and EU Taxonomy (Article 8) compliance.
quote: nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe that the Consolidated Sustainability Statements of Coöperatieve Rabobank U.A. (‘the Company’) for 2025 are not, in all material respects, prepared in accordance with the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS)
notes: The auditor adds an emphasis of matter on the high measurement uncertainty of the GHG emission figures (p. 421); the conclusion is not modified.

evidence_summary: The Dutch Public Prosecutor, which has investigated Rabobank under the AML law since December 2022, decided in April 2025 to prosecute and sent a draft indictment in December 2025. No fine or settlement was disclosed for 2025.
quote: In its press release of 9 April 2025, the DPP indicated that it has decided to summon Rabobank and that the criminal investigation is in the final phase. … In December 2025, an initial draft indictment was received.
notes: Rabobank says the impact could be significant but cannot be estimated (p. 327). The EUR 26.6 m EU competition fine (November 2023) is outside the reporting year and not ESG-related under the agreed definition. Kifid consumer-credit compensation continued in 2025 (p. 63).
